headline: At composition depth 1 the styled fold still applies, so `next-yak-9.7` leads SSR throughput just as on a flat button — the depth tax only appears once wrappers nest.

microbench.why: A single composition level still resolves to an intrinsic element, so folding removes the wrapper and `next-yak-9.7` renders at 0.442 ms/1k — its library slice is 0.09 ms. The hash runtimes trail by their per-instance naming (`styled-components` 1.15 ms/1k, `emotion` 2.12 ms/1k, `panda` 4.93 ms/1k). The 9.6.0 build rendered this at 1.12 ms/1k (2.5× slower), before folding and the perf runtime shipped as defaults.

autocannon.why: The folded lane serves the most requests, clearing `vanilla`; `panda` (173 req/s) and `emotion` (450 req/s) re-serialize per request.

attribution.why: Folded, the styled lane's library slice is 0.09 ms and its render undercuts `vanilla`. The runtime libraries carry the cost in their slice — `styled-components` 0.478 ms, `emotion` 0.888 ms, `panda` 4.75 ms of component self-time.

hydrate.why: The css-prop fold and `vanilla` hydrate fastest at ~45-47 ms with a static sheet. The styled lane sits higher here (84.1 ms), above its own fast hydration on the deeper compose cases — the composed wrapper does more client work at this shape — while the runtime libraries reflow their injected sheet (`goober` 131 ms, `emotion` 107 ms).

inp.why: Updating one composed element is ~7-8 ms for the whole field within the interaction spread — a tie the runtime libraries join at this depth because a single re-render regenerates little. Only `panda` (21.4 ms) stays back.

mount.why: The folded lane mounts with the extracted cluster (~66 ms); the runtime libraries add first-inject (`styled-components` 97.3 ms, `emotion` 99.8 ms).

renderTiming.why: One style recalc for every approach — parity; the styleMs spread is sub-millisecond.

payload.why: The css-prop fold ships smallest (2.67 kB gz), the styled lane 3.77 kB; the runtime and utility lanes are 3.6-4.3× larger (`emotion` 15.4 kB, `styled-components` 16.0 kB).

nsweep.why: At 4000 depth-1 elements the folded lane stays flat with react-dom (1.81 ms); the hash libraries compound (`styled-components` 4.62 ms, `emotion` 8.64 ms, `panda` 22.0 ms).

crossCase: `compose-1`, `compose-3` and `compose-6` are the depth sweep. At depth 1 the fold applies and `next-yak-9.7` leads exactly as on `realistic-button`; from depth 3 the styled fold can no longer resolve the element across the `styled(Component)` chain, so the win passes to the perf runtime (which flattens the wrapper chain) and to the css-prop fold (which merges the whole chain into one class).
